label: winner or champion of
definition: The first entity won the competition or award designated by the second, or held its championship title.
scope_notes: Win/champion/victory dominates. Preserve the earlier competition/award scope: historical wins and championship designations qualify, but participation, mere medal receipt without championship, winning an individual stage, and political officeholding do not. Winning the White House is a competing political meaning rather than an expansion of this predicate.

facts.reason: Kingdom is explicitly an Olympic champion in two constructions. The medalist row alone would not prove championship, but the champion paths do.
Democrats winning the White House concerns political office/control, outside the preserved competition-title and award predicate.
Aung San Suu Kyi explicitly wins the Nobel Peace Prize.

Winning the White House and attending its ceremony describe political office/event involvement, not an award or championship. The generic Democrat identity is additionally underspecified but cannot fix the predicate mismatch.
Both direct and relative-clause paths explicitly say Tabasco Cat wins the Preakness.
